modules.title: Boards

modules.title: Sharing and ACLs

spiral_refs.note: User scoping from Beginner M7 is the foundation — sharing extends ownership to multiple users

spiral_refs.preview: Federation extends the sharing model across instances — Advanced M3 builds directly on it

Keyboard navigation and focus management. Accessibility in practice — ARIA live regions for dynamic pin lists, focus trapping in modals.

The component structure from I-03 is extended with the board sidebar and action menus here

modules.title: REST API Design

spiral_refs.note: Controllers from Beginner M3 become versioned API endpoints here

modules.title: Security

spiral_refs.preview: CSP, rate limiting, audit logging, and supply chain security are the Advanced extension

cross_track_ref.note: ExApp auth handshake and request signature verification is a different but parallel security topic

advanced.title: Advanced

modules.title: Nextcloud Internals
modules.description: The full bootstrap sequence from HTTP request to controller call. DI container internals — how constructor parameters are resolved, lazy proxies, named parameters like $userId. OC_Hook legacy system vs IEventDispatcher. How Nextcloud's classloader maps namespaces to directories.

spiral_refs.note: The app bootstrap class you wrote at Beginner M2 — now you'll see exactly how Nextcloud calls it
DI from Beginner M3 gets its full internal explanation here — including why $userId resolves by name
The OCP boundary from Intermediate I-01 makes sense once you see how the container resolves services

modules.title: Event-Driven Architecture
modules.description: IEventDispatcher — publishing and subscribing to events. Designing Pinboard event classes for board creation, pin addition, and share changes. Decoupling notifications, activity, and search indexing from controller logic so they listen independently. Avoiding circular dependencies in event handlers.

spiral_refs.note: Notifications from I-06 are currently wired directly to controllers — events decouple them here
The background digest job from I-09 becomes an event subscriber rather than a polling loop
Search indexing from I-10 can react to board and pin events rather than being called directly

cross_track_ref.note: ExApps receive events via webhook callbacks rather than in-process listeners — a useful contrast

modules.title: Federation
modules.description: The OCM protocol, implementing ICloudFederationProvider for Pinboard boards. Sharing a board with a user on a remote Nextcloud instance, remote user identity and trust boundaries. Handling incoming share notifications and syncing pin activity across instances.

spiral_refs.note: The sharing model from I-04 extends across instance boundaries here
The REST API from I-07 is the transport layer for OCM notifications
Cross-instance notifications — alice on one server notified when bob on another adds a pin

cross_track_ref.note: ExApp federation counterpart — both sides implement OCM; the capstone connects them

modules.title: Real-Time and Collaborative Features
modules.description: Server-Sent Events (SSE) and long-polling to push live updates to shared boards — new pins appear without refresh. Dashboard widget showing recent activity across all boards. URL preview data fetching as a background job triggered on pin creation, with Open Graph metadata stored and surfaced in the UI. The limits of Nextcloud's notification polling mechanism.

spiral_refs.note: The Pinia store from I-03 is what SSE events update — reactive state already in place
Notifications from I-06 are extended into real-time delivery here
Background jobs from I-09 are the mechanism for async URL preview fetching
The optimistic update patterns from I-12 interact with SSE — both can update the same store

modules.title: Files and Storage Internals
modules.description: The storage abstraction stack (IStorage, Jail, Wrapper). File attachments on pins — storing files in the user's Nextcloud rather than as blobs. Mount points and file IDs across mounts, why you can't trust paths alone. Chunked upload handling. WebDAV from the frontend for direct file operations.

spiral_refs.note: The storage mention in Beginner M4 glossed over this — here's the full stack
File attachments inherit the board's share ACLs — the permission model extends to files here

cross_track_ref.note: ExApps access files via WebDAV — understanding the storage stack explains why certain things behave unexpectedly

modules.title: Caching and Distributed State
modules.description: ICacheFactory in depth — local, distributed, and Redis-backed caches and when to use each. Distributed locking with ILockingProvider for concurrent board edits (two users adding a pin simultaneously). Cache invalidation strategies for board membership and share ACLs. IMemcache vs ICache — the distinction that matters under load.

spiral_refs.note: N+1 fixes from I-13 are the prerequisite — caching only helps queries that are already correct
Share ACL lookups are the most cache-worthy queries — invalidation must be correct when shares change

modules.title: Scalability and Multi-Instance
modules.description: How Nextcloud handles horizontal scaling — stateless vs stateful components. The filecache table at scale and why large queries against it are dangerous. Object storage (S3/Swift) implications for file attachments on pins. Designing board and pin queries to be safe at 10M+ rows.

spiral_refs.note: N+1 fixes from I-13 — now stress-tested against 10M-row scenarios
The original QBMapper queries from Beginner M4 are the subject of the production-scale audit here
Distributed locking from A-06 is what prevents race conditions at this scale

cross_track_ref.note: ExApp horizontal scaling has different concerns — stateless service vs stateful PHP process

modules.title: Security Hardening
modules.description: Content Security Policy builder, ISecureRandom vs ICrypto — when to use each. Capability-based access control patterns. Rate limiting on share creation and public board endpoints with IRateLimiter. Audit logging for share events. Supply chain — evaluating JS dependencies, composer security advisories, REUSE compliance.

spiral_refs.note: The Intermediate security checklist is the baseline — this module hardens it to production posture
Share creation and public board endpoints are the rate limiting targets here
User scoping from Beginner is now evaluated against OWASP Top 10

cross_track_ref.note: ExApp supply chain includes the container image — different but parallel hardening exercise

modules.title: Contributing Upstream
modules.description: Reading and navigating the Nextcloud server codebase. The backport process and stable branch rules. Writing a compelling RFC or GitHub discussion. Working with the public API committee — what gets into OCP and what doesn't. Running the full Nextcloud test suite locally.

spiral_refs.note: Understanding what gets into OCP — from I-01 — is the prerequisite for proposing additions
Nextcloud Internals from A-01 is essential context for navigating the server codebase

cross_track_ref.note: Contributing to AppAPI itself is the ExApp parallel — same process, different codebase

modules.title: CI/CD and App Quality
modules.description: GitHub Actions for Nextcloud apps — the standard workflow templates. Automated compatibility testing across Nextcloud versions. Psalm with Nextcloud stubs, PHP-CS-Fixer, ESLint, and Stylelint. App store release automation. REUSE compliance in CI.

spiral_refs.note: The test suite from I-14 gets wired into the CI matrix here
Manual app store release from Beginner M8 becomes fully automated here

modules.title: Architecture Patterns for Complex Apps
modules.description: When to split Pinboard into multiple apps — board app vs pin app — and the library app pattern for shared code. Sidecar processes and IPC. Zero-downtime migrations for apps with active installs. Migrating from autoincrement to SnowflakeAwareEntity primary keys on a table with existing data. The decision framework for when an app should become an ExApp. Closes with a self-directed extensions section pointing to bonus module candidates.

spiral_refs.note: Packaging from Beginner M8 — now applied to a breaking schema change with 10k active installs
OCP versioning from I-01 underpins safe multi-app API design
The autoincrement primary keys from Beginner M4 get migrated to Snowflake IDs here

extensions.title: Notes on Pins and Boards

cross_track_ref.note: PHP calls INotificationManager directly — ExApp sends notifications via nc_py_api OCS wrapper. Same notification model, same user experience

modules.title: REST API Design
modules.description: Exposing your own versioned API endpoints from the ExApp for boards and pins. OCS response format, API versioning, authentication for external callers. Registering endpoints with AppAPI so Nextcloud proxies them correctly. Note: unlike PHP apps, ExApps do not use the IInitialState mechanism — initial data is fetched via a standard API call on component mount, consistent with the ExApp stateless service model.

spiral_refs.note: Request lifecycle from Beginner M2 — now exposing your own versioned endpoints

spiral_refs.preview: Federation uses this API as transport — Advanced A-03 builds directly on it

cross_track_ref.note: Same OCS contract — PHP implements it via controllers, ExApp implements it via FastAPI/Flask routes registered with AppAPI

modules.title: Files Integration
modules.description: Reading and writing user files via WebDAV and nc_py_api. File attachments on pins — storing files in the user's Nextcloud rather than in the sidecar DB. Understanding file IDs across mounts and handling permissions correctly.

spiral_refs.preview: Chunked upload/download and streaming large files without buffering is Advanced A-05

cross_track_ref.note: PHP accesses files via the storage abstraction stack — ExApp uses WebDAV. Understanding the PHP internals explains WebDAV behaviour that can otherwise seem mysterious

modules.title: Background and Async Tasks
modules.description: Async processing within your Python service using asyncio or task queues. Webhooks from Nextcloud triggering async work. Progress reporting back to the UI. Exercise: async URL preview fetching triggered on pin creation.

spiral_refs.preview: AI task processing is the ExApp killer feature for async work — Advanced A-02
Real-time progress reporting from long-running tasks is an Advanced pattern

cross_track_ref.note: PHP uses Nextcloud's cron-based job queue — ExApp owns its own async runtime. Very different operationally, same outcome

modules.title: Search
modules.description: Registering a search provider from an ExApp via nc_py_api. Indexing boards and pins in unified search, scoping results to boards the requesting user can access. Handling search from an external service — latency considerations.

spiral_refs.note: Search results must respect the share ACLs from I-04

spiral_refs.preview: Search performance at scale and caching search results is an Advanced concern

cross_track_ref.note: Same ISearchProvider concept — PHP registers it in-process, ExApp registers it via nc_py_api callback

modules.title: Settings and Admin Panel
modules.description: Serving admin and personal settings panels from your ExApp, reading and writing instance configuration via nc_py_api. Exercise: admin toggle to disable public board sharing instance-wide.

spiral_refs.note: The public sharing toggle gates the public board share feature from I-04

spiral_refs.preview: Instance-wide config interacts with horizontal scaling — Advanced A-05

cross_track_ref.note: PHP settings use ISettings directly — ExApp serves the panel HTML from the external service but registers identically

modules.title: Frontend Performance and UX
modules.description: Lazy-loading Vue components with defineAsyncComponent. Optimistic updates with rollback when the Python service rejects a change. Pagination and infinite scroll for large pin lists. Debouncing search input. Skeleton loading states.

spiral_refs.note: The Vue component from Beginner M6 gets the optimistic update pattern properly implemented here
The Pinia store from I-03 is what optimistic updates and rollbacks modify

spiral_refs.preview: Real-time UI patterns extend the reactive update model built here

cross_track_ref.note: Identical module — Vue performance patterns are the same regardless of backend

modules.title: Backend Performance
modules.description: Connection pooling to Nextcloud OCS APIs, caching strategies for share ACL lookups and board membership, avoiding redundant API calls with local sidecar DB as cache. Profiling the Python service. N+1 detection on board+pin queries.

spiral_refs.note: The sidecar DB queries from Beginner M4 are the subject of the N+1 audit here

spiral_refs.preview: Horizontal scaling changes all caching assumptions — Advanced A-05

cross_track_ref.note: PHP performance is dominated by DB query patterns — ExApp performance is dominated by OCS API call overhead and connection pooling

modules.title: Testing
modules.description: Testing ExApp business logic independently of Nextcloud — unit tests for board and pin logic, mock nc_py_api. Integration testing against a live Nextcloud instance. Testing share ACL enforcement. Frontend testing with Jest.

spiral_refs.note: The request lifecycle from Beginner M2 is what integration tests exercise

spiral_refs.preview: CI pipeline wires these tests into automated multi-version matrix testing at Advanced

cross_track_ref.note: PHP testing mocks Nextcloud services in-process — ExApp can test its service layer completely without Nextcloud, which is a significant advantage

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.tagline: Master AppAPI internals, AI integration, federation, and production scale
advanced.persona: Has shipped an ExApp, wants deeper AppAPI knowledge, real-time features, AI provider integration, or large-scale deployment confidence
advanced.app_state: Pinboard ExApp with federation, real-time board updates, AI-powered pin tagging, file attachments, production-hardened security and performance

modules.title: AppAPI Internals
modules.description: How the daemon model works under the hood — the full signing protocol, request routing, failure modes, and recovery. How registration flows from occ through the daemon to your service. Lazy ExApp loading and capability negotiation.

spiral_refs.note: Registration from Beginner M1 — now you understand the full protocol behind it
Auth handshake from Beginner M2 gets its full protocol-level explanation here
Security treatment from I-01 — now you understand what you were protecting against at the protocol level

cross_track_ref.note: PHP internals covers the server bootstrap — AppAPI internals is the ExApp equivalent view of the same boundary

modules.title: AI and Task Processing
modules.description: Implementing TaskProcessingProvider, SpeechToText, TextToImage, and ContextChat from an ExApp. AI-powered pin tagging — automatically categorise new pins into boards using a language model. The async task processing lifecycle.

spiral_refs.note: Async task patterns from I-09 are the foundation AI providers run on
Boards from Intermediate M2 are what AI auto-tagging assigns new pins to

modules.title: Federation
modules.description: OCM from a Python ExApp — implementing the federation protocol to share Pinboard boards across Nextcloud instances. Cross-instance data exchange via nc_py_api, remote user identity trust boundaries, incoming share handling.

spiral_refs.note: The sharing model from I-04 extends across instance boundaries here
The REST API from I-07 is the transport layer for OCM notifications
Cross-instance notifications — alice on one server notified when bob on another adds a pin

cross_track_ref.note: PHP federation counterpart — both implement OCM; the capstone connects them

downloads.label: Download Pinboard PHP — Federation Starting Point
downloads.description: The PHP Pinboard counterpart to federate against if you haven't done the PHP track

downloads.label: Download Federation Lab Docker Compose
downloads.description: Two pre-wired Nextcloud instances ready for the federation exercise

modules.title: Real-Time and Collaborative Features
modules.description: Server-Sent Events from a Python service to push live board updates — new pins appear without refresh. Dashboard widget showing recent board activity. Progress reporting for AI task processing. The interaction between SSE, the Pinia store, and optimistic updates.

spiral_refs.note: The Pinia store from I-03 is what SSE events update
Notifications from I-06 extended into real-time delivery
Optimistic update patterns from I-12 interact with SSE — both update the same store

cross_track_ref.note: Same SSE patterns — PHP serves them from Nextcloud itself, ExApp serves them from the Python service

modules.title: Multi-Instance Deployment and Scaling
modules.description: Running the ExApp as a horizontally scaled service — stateless design, load balancer considerations, sidecar DB becomes distributed. Redis for shared cache and session state across instances. Object storage for file attachments. When the sidecar DB model breaks down.

spiral_refs.note: Sidecar DB from Beginner M5 — now you need to make it distributed or replace it
Performance caching from I-13 breaks under horizontal scaling if not designed carefully
Instance-wide config interacts with scaling — which instance handles which request?

cross_track_ref.note: PHP scalability concerns are about the Nextcloud server itself — ExApp scalability is about your own service. Different problems, complementary concerns

modules.title: Security Hardening
modules.description: Container image supply chain — base image selection, dependency scanning, SBOM generation. Secrets management — never bake credentials into images. CSP implications of an external service serving assets. Rate limiting on share creation and public board endpoints. Runtime security and least-privilege containerisation.

spiral_refs.note: Auth hardening from I-01 is the application-level baseline — this module covers the infrastructure layer
Share creation and public board endpoints are the rate limiting targets here

cross_track_ref.note: PHP security hardening covers CSP and audit logging — ExApp adds container and secrets concerns on top

modules.title: Caching and Distributed State
modules.description: Caching OCS API responses to avoid redundant Nextcloud calls — share ACL lookups, user group membership, board metadata. Redis as a shared cache across scaled instances. Cache invalidation via Nextcloud webhook events. When to cache and when to always re-fetch.

spiral_refs.note: N+1 fixes and caching from I-13 — now applied at scale with distributed Redis
Share ACL lookups are the most cache-worthy — invalidation must be correct when shares change
Horizontal scaling from A-05 makes distributed caching a correctness concern, not just a performance one

cross_track_ref.note: PHP caches inside Nextcloud's ICacheFactory — ExApp caches OCS API responses in its own Redis. Different implementation, same invalidation challenges

modules.title: Event-Driven Architecture
modules.description: Receiving Nextcloud events via webhook callbacks — file events, user events, share events. Designing the ExApp as an event-driven service: decoupling board notifications, search indexing, and AI tagging into independent event handlers. Webhook reliability, retries, and idempotency.

spiral_refs.note: Notifications from I-06 become event-driven here rather than directly wired to API handlers
Background tasks from I-09 become event subscribers
Search indexing from I-10 reacts to board and pin events rather than being called directly

cross_track_ref.note: PHP uses IEventDispatcher in-process — ExApp receives events via HTTP webhook callbacks. Same decoupling goal, very different architecture

modules.title: CI/CD for ExApps
modules.description: Docker image builds for multiple architectures (amd64, arm64). Automated AppAPI registration testing against a real Nextcloud instance in CI. App store release automation. Container image signing and attestation. SBOM generation in the pipeline.

spiral_refs.note: Tests from I-14 get wired into the CI matrix here
Manual Docker packaging from Beginner M8 becomes a fully automated multi-arch pipeline here

cross_track_ref.note: PHP CI produces signed zips — ExApp CI produces multi-arch Docker images. Worth comparing pipelines side by side

modules.title: Contributing Upstream
modules.description: Contributing to AppAPI itself — new provider interfaces, capability additions, nc_py_api improvements, and the AppAPI release process. Navigating the AppAPI codebase, writing good issues, and the PR review process.

spiral_refs.note: AppAPI internals from A-01 is the prerequisite for knowing where to contribute
The REST API patterns from I-07 inform what good API design looks like when proposing new AppAPI endpoints

cross_track_ref.note: PHP upstream contribution targets nextcloud/server — ExApp contribution targets nextcloud/app_api and nextcloud/nc_py_api

modules.title: Architecture Patterns for Complex ExApps
modules.description: When to split an ExApp into multiple services. The sidecar service pattern for heavy computation (AI inference, image processing). Migrating from SQLite to Postgres in a sidecar DB with live users. The decision framework for when an ExApp should become a PHP app or vice versa. Closes with a self-directed extensions section.

spiral_refs.note: Packaging from Beginner M8 — now applied to a breaking schema change with live users
Data patterns from I-02 — now evaluated at production scale with migration constraints
Scaling decisions from A-05 inform when to split services

cross_track_ref.note: PHP architecture patterns cover multi-app splits — ExApp patterns cover multi-service splits. The decision framework at the end of both modules explicitly compares the two approaches

extensions.description: Post pin activity to Talk rooms via the Talk bot API from the Python service.

standalone.description: Self-contained single-topic modules. Each can be taken independently of any track. Tagged beginner, intermediate, or advanced to indicate assumed knowledge level.

modules.title: Setting Up Your Development Environment
modules.description: Step-by-step installation guide for the Nextcloud development environment — Docker Desktop, nextcloud-docker-dev bootstrap, nvm, and Node.js — for macOS, Ubuntu, Windows, and GitHub Codespaces. Intended for developers who have not set up a Nextcloud dev environment before.

modules.title: Dev Environment Deep Dive
modules.description: Xdebug setup and step debugging, profiling, advanced log analysis, and Docker-dev tips that don't fit in the track M1.

modules.title: Git Workflow for Nextcloud
modules.description: Backports, stable branches, PR conventions, commit message format, and how the Nextcloud release cycle affects your contributions.

modules.title: l10n and i18n
modules.description: Translation workflow, Transifex, plural forms, `t()` vs `n()`, and how to structure strings for translators.

modules.title: REUSE and Licensing Compliance
modules.description: SPDX headers, the REUSE spec, reuse tooling for automated compliance checks, and what licence choices are compatible with Nextcloud apps.

modules.title: Writing Good Tests
modules.description: Testing patterns specific to Nextcloud beyond the basics — integration test fixtures, database rollbacks, testing background jobs, and end-to-end Cypress setup.

modules.title: Static Analysis with Psalm
modules.description: Psalm setup for Nextcloud apps, Nextcloud stubs, fixing common errors, baseline workflow, and integrating into CI.

modules.title: Accessibility in Nextcloud Apps
modules.description: WCAG requirements, keyboard navigation, screen reader testing, ARIA roles in Vue components, and using @nextcloud/vue correctly to get accessibility for free.

modules.title: Taint Analysis and Security Annotations
modules.description: `@psalm-taint-source`, `@psalm-taint-sink`, `@psalm-taint-escape` — tracing user input through controllers to DB and output, and how Nextcloud's own annotations work.

modules.title: App Store Submission
modules.description: Code signing, the app store review process, maintaining a listing, responding to issues, and planning releases around Nextcloud's release cycle.

modules.title: Maintaining Compatibility
modules.description: Supporting multiple Nextcloud versions simultaneously, deprecation handling, version-gated code, and building a multi-version CI test matrix.

modules.title: Nextcloud Design System
modules.description: The Nextcloud HIG, CSS variables, when to use which @nextcloud/vue component, icon conventions, and design review process for app store submissions.

modules.title: Theming Your App
modules.description: Custom themes, dark mode testing, RTL support, and ensuring your app looks correct across all Nextcloud theme variants.

modules.title: Understanding Federation
modules.description: Conceptual introduction to federation — what it means, how OCM works, what users experience, and what it means for app developers. No code.

modules.title: AppAPI vs PHP Apps — When to Choose What
modules.description: Decision guide covering the tradeoffs between the two approaches — language, deployment, performance, maintenance, and App Store implications.

modules.title: GDPR Compliance for App Developers
modules.description: `IAccountManager`, data export hooks, account deletion cleanup, retention policies, and what your app must implement to be compliant with GDPR requirements.

modules.title: Contributing to Nextcloud Libraries
modules.description: Local dev setup for Nextcloud libraries, Storybook for @nextcloud/vue, component API design conventions, and the PR process across nextcloud-vue, @nextcloud/axios, @nextcloud/router, and @nextcloud/dialogs.

modules.title: Smart Picker Provider
modules.description: Register your app as a Smart Picker provider — implement ISearchProvider and a reference provider so pins and boards can be searched, inserted as rich links, and rendered inline across Nextcloud apps including Text, Talk, Deck, and Notes. Covers the provider lifecycle, custom result rendering, and admin settings for API credentials.
